title: Six plural arrangements, each read by the format it belongs to

census.why: gettext, read end to end. `claimRatio` of 1.0 is the point and not a detail: `sweep` only calls an oracle hit a CONFIRMED miss when the ratio is 1 under a measured extractor, so a format read this way can contradict the engine, while one left to the residual sweep can only ever produce candidates.

Fluent, and the only arrangement in the corpus that genuinely costs a parser. Its selector is a grammar with nesting, a mandatory default variant and two kinds of variant key; no table of separators reads one. Two grammars ship in this engine and every other arrangement is a data row, which is the shape of the claim the design makes.

An XML plist, read by the markup extractor — but only because that extractor now gives a plist dict a JSON Pointer. Registering the extension alone would have produced `string/text[7]`, a document-order index carrying no key, and which key owns a value is exactly what an Apple plural is made of.
The counter-example, and the argument for the whole design: registering one extension turned an unreadable file into a dialect ROW. The engine gained an arrangement without gaining a detector.

The nastiest path in the corpus, and now the tidiest result. `.ts` is TypeScript and it is also Qt Linguist; the file used to go to the TypeScript grammar, report nineteen unparseable regions and land on `claimRatio` 0 — a broken module where there is a perfectly good catalog. Sniffed for `<!DOCTYPE TS>` before the extension decides, which is the one collision worth a content check.

expectations.why: A msgid is simultaneously the source copy and the LOOKUP KEY every catalog in the repository indexes on. Rewrite it without rewriting every `.po` in lockstep and every lookup breaks; leave it and a source-language swap keeps English msgids, which is how most projects run gettext. Two correct answers, one of which fails at runtime — so the engine reports and refuses rather than choosing.

The indexed form, in a French catalog during an en→ru run: copy, plainly, and none of this run's business. `other-locale-bundle` and not `code-token` — calling a French sentence a token is the sort of small lie that makes a report stop being worth reading. Its number is a POSITION, which is what the family below records.

The rule TODO §1 recorded as unable to fire. `**/*.ftl` was in its globs all along; what blocked it was that `classify` short-circuits on sweep sites before `matchRules` ever runs, so a format with no extractor can never reach a rule that names it. Giving Fluent a reader is what switched the rule on — no rule was edited.
A form inside the variable dictionary, addressed as `/task_count/tasks/other` rather than as the eighth text run in the document.

French text during an en→ru run, so the detector refuses — correctly, and that refusal is unrelated to the arrangement. What matters here is that the site EXISTS, at `message[0]/numerusform[1]`, where before it was a fragment swept out of a file the grammar had choked on.
CLAIMED, unlike everything else in this case, because `.xcstrings` is registered as JSON and a data row reads the resulting path. One line in an extension set and one row in a catalog.

plurals.why: The original counter-example: registering one extension turned an unreadable file into a data row. It is now one of six rather than the only one.

Claimed at precedence 26, not by `rails.sibling-object` at 40 — and the difference is the whole reason the row exists. The Rails row would read `/task_count/tasks/one` correctly, but only while `bundleOnly` passes, and here it passes only because the path happens to contain `en.lproj`. A `.stringsdict` at `Resources/` would be missed entirely. Intrinsic evidence and an Apple citation beat a coincidence.

`replace` is earned rather than convenient: en→ru turns two variants into four inside a single value, which no delimiter join can do. It also has to be earned in code — a `replace` family with no serializer falls through to a `|`-join, and for Fluent that overwrites valid syntax with prose.

`cldr: false`, so the index is a POSITION and the family is never measured for completeness — index 1 of a three-form Polish catalog is 'the second form', never `few`. That also makes `insert` safe: with the target keeping the source's arity, every form already exists and is replaced at its own byte offset, so nothing is ever inserted.

Anchored on the enclosing <message>, not on a document-order text index. That is what makes a second message a second family rather than four forms of one — the failure a flat `numerusform/text[n]` path would have produced silently.

Was claimed by `vue-i18n.pipe-positional` as three positional forms. Same categories, different dialect, and the difference is not cosmetic: positional says 'first, second, third' while `{0}`, `]0,1]` and `]1,Inf[` say zero, one, other for a reason each part states. The interval knowledge lives in the Symfony row rather than as a guard inside vue-i18n's, because one runtime's spelling inside another's dialect is the coupling this design exists to remove. Writable now rather than `code-edit`: `partTemplate` puts each part's interval back where it was, so the value is rebuilt with its selectors instead of being rejoined with a bare pipe — which would have produced bodies and no intervals, a corrupted file rather than a degraded one.

The pair where the two readings DISAGREE, and therefore the one that proves `partSelector` is real. Two parts: read positionally they are one|other, because that is what two positions mean; read by their own selectors `{0}` and `]1,Inf[` they are zero|other. `cart_items` above happens to agree with the positional answer, so on its own it could never have shown the difference. Writable now rather than `code-edit`: `partTemplate` puts each part's interval back where it was, so the value is rebuilt with its selectors instead of being rejoined with a bare pipe — which would have produced bodies and no intervals, a corrupted file rather than a degraded one.

knownGaps: gettext's `nplurals=N` header is read verbatim and used by nothing. Comparing it against the number of `msgstr[n]` present would find a live rendering bug, and it is deliberately not done: reading half a header invites the reader to believe the whole thing is understood, and `plural=` is a C expression this engine will not evaluate.
